cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. That is below the 40 to 60% typically seen in production systems of this complexity, and it means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure for production availability. A regression that reaches production cannot be reversed without the engineer present and cannot be reversed quickly. We recommend establishing an automated or semi-automated deployment pipeline with a tested, documented rollback procedure exercised at least quarterly.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Database access rests with a single engineer on a month-to-month contract, with no documented handover procedure if that contract ends. This creates a hard dependency on one person's continued employment and availability. Any unplanned departure would leave the company unable to access its production database until credentials could be rotated, and no process exists to execute that rotation quickly. We recommend establishing a shared credential store, documenting the access-handover procedure, and moving the engineer to a longer-term contract or cross-training a second person immediately.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Retention of customer personal data is indefinite with no deletion policy in place. There is no documented process for handling data-subject deletion requests, and the company has no compensating control. This creates direct exposure under data protection regulations that require deletion on request, with no mitigation underway.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. The last 3 production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, and deployments occur manually with no documented rollback procedure. Below the 40 to 60% range typical for systems of this complexity, the current coverage leaves regressions unchallenged until they reach users. A single engineer controls each deployment, creating a bottleneck that compounds the risk when rollback becomes necessary.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, exposed to any database user or administrator without additional access control. This creates a critical vulnerability because customer authentication credentials are readable in their stored form, and a compromise of database access immediately yields valid login material for external systems. Immediate remediation is required before any further production use.

Manual deployments with no documented rollback procedure create a significant operational risk. A single engineer performs all deployments via direct server access, and the most recent attempted rollback, 6 months ago, required 4 hours to complete because the procedure had to be reconstructed from memory. Production incidents cannot be reversed with confidence or speed.

Code comment style varies across the codebase without an enforced linting rule to establish consistency. Reviewers spend time on stylistic corrections rather than logic and correctness, and new team members lack a clear standard to follow. Establishing a comment convention and enabling automated enforcement would reduce friction in code review and accelerate contributor onboarding.
